modality: pelvic MRI with structural segmentation labels
role: candidate source of UTERUS and OVARY geometry, of which this repository has zero entities
access: Zenodo record 13749613 carries NO licence field (license, rights and access_conditions all null). The terms are stated in the description's 'User Agreement': 'available for free use exclusively in non-commercial scientific research', and any publication must cite Liang et al., 'A Multi-Modal Pelvic MRI Dataset for Deep Learning-Based Pelvic Organ Segmentation in Endometriosis'. IRB: UTHealth CPHS protocol HSC-SBMI-22-0184.

verified_here.method: Zenodo REST API, 2026-09-10; zenodo.org answers 200 from this machine now
verified_here.record: 13749613, published 2024-09-11, one file UT-EndoMRI.zip of 7.98 GB
verified_here.dataset_1: D1_MHS: 51 patients, T2 and T1 fat-suppressed; uterus, ovaries, endometriomas, cysts and cul-de-sac contoured by THREE raters (files *_ut_r1.nii.gz etc.)
verified_here.dataset_2: D2_TCPW: 73 subjects in the archive (the description says 82); T1, T1FS, T2, T2FS; one rater
verified_here.caveat_from_the_record: ovaries may be deformed or ABSENT through surgical resection; MRI sequences may be missing

archive_layout.method: the zip's own central directory, read by HTTP Range from Zenodo on 2026-09-10 (listing saved as data/raw/anatomy/ut-endomri/central_directory_listing.json)
anomalies: one file named ut_re3 -- read as rater 3 and flagged
three files named pat -- meaning undocumented, excluded and flagged
rater coverage in D1 is uneven: rater 3 labelled the uterus in 47 subjects, rater 2 in 26, rater 1 in 9

pelvic_landmarks.t2_geometry: 480 x 480 x 32 voxels, 0.5 x 0.5 x 5.0 mm, LAS: 160 mm superior-inferior
pelvic_landmarks.sanity: the rater's uterus centroid lies inside the box the pelvic bones span
pelvic_landmarks.consequence: with 160 mm of coverage the femurs, and possibly the iliac crests, are CUT by the volume; bone centroids would be biased toward the scan, so registration uses one-way partial-to-whole surface fitting, not centroid correspondence

the_caution_that_belongs_on_the_face_of_: It is an ENDOMETRIOSIS cohort. Endometriosis distorts pelvic anatomy -- adhesions, endometriomas, adenomyosis, altered uterine position and ovarian morphology -- so these uteri and ovaries are not a typical-anatomy reference and must never be presented as one. Using them would mean a body whose uterus came from a patient selected for uterine pathology.
limitations: MRI segmentation of a clinical cohort, not a curated atlas. Different subject from the body's skeleton, from its skin, and from whatever supplies the breast.
corrections: the relayed 'CC-BY licence' is WRONG: there is no licence on the record, and the stated terms are non-commercial scientific research only
the second set holds 73 subjects in the archive, not the 82 the record's description states (and not the relayed 81); counted from the zip's central directory
uterus labels exist for 111 of 124 subjects and ovary labels for 101, not 'all subjects'

owner_decision.decision: The programme owner confirmed that this programme is non-commercial scientific research within the record's User Agreement ('available for free use exclusively in non-commercial scientific research').
obligations: cite Liang et al., 'A Multi-Modal Pelvic MRI Dataset for Deep Learning-Based Pelvic Organ Segmentation in Endometriosis', in any publication using it
raw data and derived geometry stay out of git (data/raw and data/derived are gitignored); nothing from this record is redistributed
the endometriosis caveat stays on every derived artefact: these uteri and ovaries come from a pathology-selected cohort and are not a typical-anatomy reference
